articles.title: Extraversion is linked to faster relief from depressive symptoms
articles.summary: During psychiatric treatment, a patient's personality and depression symptoms change in tandem. A new study reveals that high neuroticism slows recovery across multiple symptoms, while extraversion and agreeableness may help patients bounce back faster.

articles.title: Older adults tell the story of their lives differently, and it may not be a sign of decline, new psychology study suggests
articles.summary: Older adults described both one-time events and recurring routines with more general facts and fewer specific details than younger adults did, yet both age groups struggled similarly when they had to switch between memory types.

articles.title: Early fluid intelligence linked to faster gray matter refinement
articles.summary: A large longitudinal study reveals that early childhood intelligence scores can predict the pace at which gray and white matter develop during adolescence, highlighting distinct patterns of brain refinement and network specialization.

articles.title: One in three teen boys follows Andrew Tate at least a little, and those who do hold more rigid views of manhood
articles.summary: A third of U.S. teen boys in a new survey said they follow Andrew Tate at least a little. Those who did tended to favor emotional detachment, dominance, toughness, and rejecting femininity, even after accounting for their parents' messages.

articles.title: Just 3,000 steps a day may help slow Alzheimer's, scientists find
articles.summary: Walking just 3,000 steps a day could help slow Alzheimer’s-related brain changes, according to new research. Scientists discovered that physical activity was linked to less buildup of harmful tau proteins and nearly half the cognitive and functional decline, even in people already showing early signs of the disease. The strongest benefits appeared at 5,000 to 7,500 daily steps, suggesting that the popular 10,000-step goal may not be necessary.

articles.title: Brain scans map multiple “low road” fear pathways between the human thalamus and amygdala
articles.summary: Animal studies have described “low road” pathways that rush sensory information from the thalamus to the amygdala. A brain imaging study of 113 people now maps several such routes in humans, with some far more consistent than others.

articles.summary: Petting a dog after a stressful task didn’t speed recovery, but in a new experiment it was followed by calmer brain and heart responses when dog owners faced a second stress test soon after.

articles.title: Brain wave study reveals shifting auditory responses in children with ADHD
articles.summary: Children with ADHD process unexpected sounds differently than their peers, but these brain responses change as they grow. New research shows heightened sensitivity to sudden noises in early childhood gives way to blunted responses in middle childhood.

articles.title: PolyGraph: Plan-Buffered CUDA Graphs for Adaptive Speculative Decoding
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive speculative decoding changes the active batch size B and draft length d from one decode step to the next, whereas a CUDA Graph replays a fixed launch configuration. The resulting verification width M = B d forces serving systems to pre-capture many shapes, capture new ones on the serving path, or pad every step to the largest draft. We present PolyGraph, a plan-buffer mechanism for custom Triton kernels that avoids this choice. PolyGraph captures one maximum-grid graph and writes the active shape to GPU memory before each replay. Kernels

articles.title: Why some people escape Alzheimer’s despite carrying a high-risk gene
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered why some people with a high genetic risk of Alzheimer’s remain mentally sharp into their 80s, uncovering a rare mutation that protects the brain from harmful protein buildup. The findings reveal a potential new way to prevent early brain damage and could pave the way for treatments that mimic this natural defense.
